The correspondence I received from my colleague Dr. Pemberton at Oxford contained disturbing news regarding the recent excavations in the Welsh countryside. His team had uncovered what appeared to be a pre-Roman settlement, yet the artifacts they discovered bore no resemblance to any known Celtic or British culture. Most troubling of all were the stone tablets covered in hieroglyphs that seemed to shift and writhe when observed under certain lighting conditions.

Pemberton's description of the "singing chamber"--a circular room carved from solid bedrock and lined with crystals of unknown composition--reminded me uncomfortably of similar structures mentioned in the forbidden chronicles of the Comte d'Erlette. According to his letters, the chamber produced harmonic frequencies that affected both electromagnetic instruments and the mental state of anyone who remained within its confines for extended periods.
